standard_prerequisites.name: Splitting of a simplicial set
standard_prerequisites.use: Uniqueness is relative to the notion of splitting from Definition definition-split; the initial observation that N(U_m) must be the nondegenerate simplices reads off that definition.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 2012-2016): a simplicial set U has a unique splitting, and in it N(U_m) is the set of nondegenerate m-simplices.

Verification (proof lines 2018-2032): if x = U(phi)(y) = U(psi)(z) with phi: [n] -> [k], psi: [n] -> [l] surjective and y, z nondegenerate, choose a right inverse xi of psi; then z = U(xi)(x) = U(phi xi)(y), and nondegeneracy of z forces phi xi surjective, hence l >= k; symmetrically k >= l; so phi xi = id_[l] for every right inverse xi of psi, which forces psi = phi.
proof_roadmap: Unfold Definition definition-split: a splitting writes U_n as a coproduct over surjections indexed by nondegenerate simplices.
Compare two presentations of the same simplex through a right inverse of one of the surjections.
The two inequalities l >= k and k >= l identify the presentations.
difficulty_reason: Splitting uniqueness (statement 2012-2016, proof 2018-2032): the comparison argument is explicit - right inverse, two surjectivity inequalities, and identification of the surjections; the two small nameable steps (any splitting must have N(U_m) the nondegenerate simplices, definitional; phi xi = id for all right inverses forces psi = phi, two lines) are recorded in notes. H3.
